description: Creates a short link to a webinar's registration page that counts its clicks and carries the tracking parameters of its channel, so the host can put a pretty address into an invitation instead of a long one. Side effect: it adds a link to the campaign's link list and counts clicks from now on; nothing else on the campaign changes and no page is rebuilt. Needs `session_id` and `webinar_id` from wi_list_webinars. `channel` says where the link will be shared; `word` is an optional short topic word; `count` creates several links at once that differ by running number; `fields` lets a link carry a form value for one person, for example a hidden who-referred-this-person field, which is how one link per person is made. For several sources in one go pass `sources` and get one link per source. Write the returned short address out in full inside the invitation text, never a long UTM address.

count.description: How many links at once, 1 to 10. Default 1.

fields.description: Form values the link should fill in for the participant, e.g. {"wi_8": "Anna"} for a hidden field. One link per person when each carries its own value.

session_id.description: From an earlier turn (weiter · texte · stand).

site.description: Which connected site is meant when this chat has more than one: the address exactly as wi_get_connector_status lists it under sites. Leave it out while only one site is connected.

sources.description: Several sources in one call, one link per entry.

count.description: How many links for this source, 1 to 10.

fields.description: Form values this link should carry.

label.description: A name for this source, e.g. the group it goes into.

word.description: A short topic word for this link.

webinar_id.description: The webinar (campaign) id, as wi_list_webinars returned it. Never invent an id.

word.description: A short topic word of 3 to 10 letters for the address, invented to fit the topic.

name: wi_create_webinar_link
title: Create a short tracking link for a webinar
